Legendary graphic designer Susan Kare recently delivered a talk at the Startup School 2026 event. The video of her speech has been uploaded to Y Combinator's YouTube channel, and you can watch it below.

Susan Kare shared many wonderful stories and design insights.

It has been over 40 years since the original Macintosh was launched, but the system's graphics, fonts, icons, and overall UI elements still look as appealing today as they did back then.

In fact, many of the elements Susan Kare designed for the original Macintosh remain part of macOS to this day, preserved both in spirit and in appearance. From the Command key symbol and the "Happy Mac" startup icon to the system fonts and the hand-shaped cursor, Kare's work not only shaped the visual language of the Mac but also influenced the entire personal computer industry.

Although anyone who has studied Apple's history has probably seen Kare's manuscripts, and may have seen or heard her talk about these early works in interviews, listening to her share in her own words—the era when graphical user interfaces and pixel art were still uncharted territory—the passion and frustration of that work remains absolutely captivating.

So, if you're interested in design, curious about Apple's history, or simply want to hear someone share a lifelong passion from a professional perspective, Kare's talk is absolutely not to be missed.

In addition to talking in detail about her work at Apple, Kare also discussed how she came to join the company, showed some of the work she created after leaving, shared various anecdotes from Apple's early days, and quoted other legendary designers, bringing even more inspiration to the audience.
